name: Mitochondrial Complex V Deficiency (ATP Synthase Deficiency)

clinicalPearls: Complex V (F1Fo ATP synthase) is the terminal step of oxidative phosphorylation, using the proton gradient generated by Complexes I, III and IV to phosphorylate ADP to ATP; its deficiency uniquely tends to raise 3-methylglutaconic acid in the urine.

TMEM70 deficiency is the commonest nuclear cause and a defect of ATP synthase biogenesis; it produces a recognisable neonatal encephalo-cardiomyopathy with lactic acidosis, hyperammonaemia, 3-methylglutaconic aciduria and often facial dysmorphism, and is prevalent in the Roma population owing to a founder variant.

The mtDNA subunit gene MT-ATP6 is the classic maternally inherited cause: high heteroplasmy produces maternally inherited Leigh syndrome, while a somewhat lower load produces NARP (Neuropathy, Ataxia and Retinitis Pigmentosa).

NARP characteristically combines sensory neuropathy, cerebellar ataxia and pigmentary retinopathy, sometimes with seizures, dementia and proximal weakness, and severity correlates with the mutant heteroplasmy level.
MT-ATP8 variants and nuclear structural or assembly genes such as ATP5F1A, ATP5F1D, ATP5F1E and ATPAF2 are rarer causes of Complex V deficiency.

Neonatal presentations feature severe lactic acidosis, hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, hypotonia and encephalopathy, with the combination of 3-methylglutaconic aciduria and hyperammonaemia being a strong pointer to TMEM70.
In isolated Complex V deficiency the activities of the other respiratory chain complexes are typically preserved, and blue-native studies show reduced assembled ATP synthase.
Testing MT-ATP6 heteroplasmy across tissues and in maternal relatives is important for diagnosis and genetic counselling, as blood levels may underestimate the burden.
reference.pathophysiology: Complex V (F1Fo ATP synthase) is the molecular motor that completes oxidative phosphorylation: protons pumped into the intermembrane space by Complexes I, III and IV flow back through the membrane-embedded Fo domain, driving rotation that the catalytic F1 head uses to condense ADP and inorganic phosphate into ATP. The membrane proton channel is formed largely by the mtDNA-encoded subunits ATP6 and ATP8 (genes MT-ATP6 and MT-ATP8), while the F1 catalytic subunits and the many structural and biogenesis factors are nuclear-encoded. Disease results either from maternally inherited MT-ATP6 (and rarely MT-ATP8) variants that impair proton translocation and coupling, or from autosomal recessive nuclear variants in structural subunits (ATP5F1A, ATP5F1D, ATP5F1E) and biogenesis/assembly factors, most importantly TMEM70 and ATPAF2. Failure of ATP synthase both starves the cell of ATP and, by preventing dissipation of the proton gradient, hyperpolarises the inner membrane and promotes reactive oxygen species; the impaired terminal phosphorylation and disturbed intramitochondrial metabolism characteristically generate 3-methylglutaconic aciduria, and energy deficit again strikes brain, heart and muscle, with the heteroplasmy level of mtDNA variants determining whether the phenotype is NARP or the more severe maternally inherited Leigh syndrome.
additionalDifferentials: Mitochondrial Complex I deficiency (NADH:ubiquinone oxidoreductase defect)
Mitochondrial Complex III deficiency (cytochrome bc1 / BCS1L defect)
Mitochondrial Complex IV deficiency (cytochrome c oxidase / COX defect)
Other 3-methylglutaconic aciduria syndromes (Barth syndrome/TAZ, OPA3/Costeff, DNAJC19, SERAC1/MEGDEL)
Combined oxidative phosphorylation deficiencies and mtDNA maintenance defects
Other causes of neonatal lactic acidosis with hyperammonaemia (urea cycle and organic acid disorders)
Retinitis pigmentosa with ataxia from other causes for the NARP phenotype
additionalInvestigations: Blood and cerebrospinal fluid lactate and pyruvate with lactate-to-pyruvate ratio
Urine organic acids specifically seeking 3-methylglutaconic acid, and plasma ammonia
Echocardiography and electrocardiography for hypertrophic cardiomyopathy
Neuroimaging for Leigh-type basal ganglia and brainstem lesions
MT-ATP6/MT-ATP8 sequencing with heteroplasmy quantification across multiple tissues and in maternal relatives
Nuclear gene testing (TMEM70, ATPAF2, ATP5F1A, ATP5F1D, ATP5F1E) by panel or exome
Respiratory chain enzymology and blue-native electrophoresis showing isolated Complex V deficiency with reduced assembled enzyme
redFlags: Severe neonatal lactic acidosis with hyperammonaemia and hypertrophic cardiomyopathy suggesting TMEM70 deficiency
Rapidly progressive brainstem dysfunction and regression in maternally inherited Leigh syndrome
Cardiorespiratory decompensation during intercurrent illness in an affected infant
Progressive visual loss with ataxia and neuropathy indicating advancing NARP
Encephalopathy with intractable metabolic acidosis in the newborn period
reference.prognosis: Neonatal TMEM70 and severe nuclear or high-heteroplasmy MT-ATP6 (maternally inherited Leigh) presentations carry a high early mortality, though some TMEM70 survivors stabilise with residual cardiac and neurological disability; NARP tends to follow a slower, stepwise course whose severity tracks the mutant heteroplasmy level.
pitfalls: Missing 3-methylglutaconic aciduria because it is not specifically sought on the organic acid profile, thereby overlooking a key clue to Complex V deficiency.
Relying on blood-only MT-ATP6 heteroplasmy, which can underestimate the mutant load present in clinically affected tissues.
Confusing the NARP retinopathy-ataxia picture with a primary retinal dystrophy or a spinocerebellar ataxia.
Not considering TMEM70 in a dysmorphic neonate with cardiomyopathy, lactic acidosis and hyperammonaemia, particularly in at-risk founder populations.
Overlooking the other 3-methylglutaconic aciduria syndromes (such as Barth syndrome) in the differential of a boy with cardiomyopathy and neutropenia.

management: No cure; supportive mitochondrial cofactor supplementation with avoidance of fasting and catabolic stress

Treat neonatal metabolic crises with intravenous dextrose and fluids and correction of lactic acidosis, and manage the hyperammonaemia of TMEM70 disease with ammonia-scavenging agents and protein modulation
Cardiac surveillance with echocardiography and ECG and heart-failure therapy for hypertrophic cardiomyopathy
Anticonvulsants and neurological symptomatic care for Leigh-type encephalopathy and NARP-associated seizures
Support NARP manifestations with visual rehabilitation for the retinitis pigmentosa and physiotherapy for ataxia and neuropathy
Multidisciplinary follow-up spanning dietetics, cardiology, neurology and ophthalmology
Genetic counselling distinguishing autosomal recessive nuclear disease such as the TMEM70 founder variant from maternally inherited MT-ATP6 disease with heteroplasmy-dependent recurrence risk
